name: Sowmya Narayana Perumal Temple, Thirukoshtiyur
deity: Vishnu as Sowmya Narayana Perumal, with the Goddess Thirumamagal — worshipped reclining, standing and seated on the three levels of the vimana
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country, sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham and hallowed by Ramanuja
summary: At Thirukoshtiyur, beneath a vimana taller than its own gateway, Vishnu is worshipped as Sowmya Narayana — the temple from which, tradition holds, Ramanuja proclaimed the sacred mantra to all.

sections.history: Thirukoshtiyur is a village in Sivaganga district, near Tiruppattur, whose temple of Sowmya Narayana Perumal is one of the 108 Divya Desams of the Pandya Nadu, praised by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. It is above all the village of Thirukoshtiyur Nambi, one of the teachers of Ramanuja. Sri Vaishnava tradition tells that Ramanuja, sent here by Thirukachi Nambi, walked to Thirukoshtiyur again and again to receive the eight-syllabled mantra, Om Namo Narayanaya, and was turned away seventeen times before Nambi at last taught him, under a vow of secrecy. Ramanuja then climbed the temple and proclaimed the mantra to everyone gathered below, whatever their birth. Shrines to both Nambi and Ramanuja stand within the temple.
sections.architecture: The temple is remarkable for its Ashtanga vimana, which rises higher than the five-tiered rajagopuram at the entrance. The vimana is built in three levels, each a shrine: on the ground the lord reclines, on the second he stands as Devaloka Perumal, and on the third he is seated as Vaikunta Perumal. The upper levels are reached by stairs, and from the vimana devotees see the place where Ramanuja is said to have stood. The Goddess Thirumamagal has her own shrine.
sections.legends: The name is said to recall a koshti, a gathering: tradition holds that the devas assembled here to take counsel with Vishnu, and so the place became Thirukoshtiyur. But the story every visitor hears is Ramanuja's — of a teacher who guarded the mantra and a disciple who, accepting that he himself might suffer for breaking his word, chose to share the path to liberation with all who would listen.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava festivals, above all Vaikunta Ekadashi, with processions of the utsava deities through the village. The days of Ramanuja and of Thirukoshtiyur Nambi are honoured with special worship and the recitation of the Divya Prabandham, recalling the event that made this shrine famous.
sections.experience: Climb the vimana to stand where tradition places Ramanuja's proclamation, and look out over the village and its fields. Each level of the tower brings a fresh darshan — reclining, standing, seated — making a visit here unlike most temples. The village is quiet; combine it with Karaikudi and the Chettinad country close by.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi is busiest. Confirm current timings, including access to the upper vimana shrines, before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukoshtiyur lies near Tiruppattur in Sivaganga district, reached by road from Tiruppattur, Sivaganga or Karaikudi. Karaikudi and Sivaganga have the nearest railway stations, and Madurai Airport, about 70 km away, is the nearest airport.
